question.text: A UNIQUE feature of Cat III AIFs (versus Cat I and Cat II) is that Cat III can be structured as:

answer.text: Perpetual with no maturity in any form

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the SEBI (AIF) Regulations, Cat I and Cat II must be close-ended. Cat III has the option to be structured as either open-ended or close-ended. This optional structure is the defining feature of Cat III relative to the other categories. The Trap: Close-ended-only (A) describes Cat I/II, not Cat III's defining flexibility. Open-ended-only (B) overstates the rule. Perpetual structures (D) are not contemplated under the regulations for AIFs. Note: The open-ended/close-ended structural distinction across categories is set out in the workbook on pp. 125 and 391.
